correctness.rationale: For relative-character order four, Haar pushes to uniform {1,i,-1,-i}. With s=p/2>1 and balance t=2|a||b|/sum magnitudes squares, norm^p/energy^{s} equals [g_s(t cos phi)+g_s(t sin phi)]/2, g_s(u)=((1+u)^s+(1-u)^s)/2. Since g_s strictly increases for positive arguments, the maximum has t=1, equal coefficient magnitudes. Phase derivative on (0,pi/4) is cos(phi)sin(phi)[q_s(sin phi)-q_s(cos phi)]/2 with q_s(u)=g_s'(u)/u a positive multiple of the centered interval average of (1+x)^{s-2}. This average increases in radius for s in (1,2) or (3,infinity), decreases for (2,3), and is flat at s=2,3 by strict convexity/concavity. Thus axis/diagonal/axis phase classes, transitions p=4,6, and exact endpoint constants follow. Numerical independent endpoint comparisons confirm representative regimes but proof covers every real p>2.
